2. The Kingston Springs Volunteer Fire Department. The purpose of these Emergency Assistance Policies and Procedures is to establish guidelines that will govern the above parties in the process of responding to the request of the other party hereto for emergency assistance or in requesting emergency assistance from the other party hereto. The following sections establish the guidelines under which decisions and their extent of implementation will be made regarding emergency assistance. a) “Emergency Assistance” shall mean fire fighting assistance, emergency medical assistance or any other emergency assistance provided by either party. | | b) “Requesting party” shall mean the fire department which requests | emergency assistance. | c) “Responding party” shall mean the fire department which responds to a request for emergency assistance. d) “Responsible party” shall mean the party in whose jurisdiction the incident occurs. e) “Appropriate senior officer” shall mean the chief of the fire department or his designee. 2s R For Emer, i a) All requests for emergency assistance shall be made or authorized by the appropriate senior officer. Pursuant to TCA, § 58-2-606, the senior officer of the requesting party on the scene of the emergency shall be in command of the emergency as to strategy, | tactics and overall direction of the operation. All orders or directions regarding the operation of the responding party shall be relayed to the senior officer in command of the responding party.
b) qd) The requesting party shall not be liable for damages to the equipment or personnel of the responding party in responding to a request for emergency assistance. Neither the requesting party nor its employees shall be liable for any damages caused by the negligence of the personnel of the responding party while in route to or returning from its scene of the emergency. Neither the responding party nor its employees shall be liable for any property damage or bodily injury at the actual scene of any emergency due to actions which are performed in responding to a request for emergency assistance. Neither party has a duty to respond to a request for emergency assistance and may reject the request or depart from the scene of the emergency at any time at the discretion of the officer in command of the responding party at the scene of the emetgency. R jing TO AR ForE Upon receipt of a request for aid as provided for in the preceding paragraphs, the responding party may respond as follows: a) b) One (1) piece of equipment and crew may be sent to the location requested. Any request for additional equipment or personnel by the requesting party will be made to the senior officer of the responding party at the scene, who will evaluate the needs and make any request to his appropriate senior officer. A chief officer may respond if equipment is sent to the emergency scene. The total response provided shall be determined by the ranking officer of the responding party. In cases where two (2) or more requests for emergency assistance are made at the same time, the appropriate senior officer shall determine based upon a reasonable appraisal of the emergencies of the requesting parties, how best to respond to the requests. The appropriate senior officer may determine to send all available resources to the jurisdiction with the more dire emergency or may send some resources to each requesting party. ARCHIVE
The employees of each fire department shall have extended to any geographical area necessary as a result of a request for emergency assistance, the same authority, rights, privileges and immunities including coverage under line-of-duty injury and sickness leave, which they have within their jurisdictional limits. Either party may abandon these Emergency Assistance Policies and Procedures upon not less than thirty (30) days advance written notice to the other party. After such abandonment, neither party shall have any further obligations or responsibilities relating to these Emergency Assistance Policies and Procedures. These Emergency Assistance Policies and Procedures are being adopted pursuant to the authority of the Local Government Emergency Assistance Act of 1987 (TCA, §§ 58-2-601 through 58-2-609) and TCA, § 6-21-703. These Emergency Assistance Policies and Procedures shall not be binding upon ~ the parties until signed by all necessary officials, filed in the office of the Metropolitan Clerk, approved by the Metropolitan Council by ordinance and assigned a Metropolitan Contract Number. In Witness Whereof, the parties have caused these Emergency Assistance Policies and Procedures to be executed on the separate signature pages as of the am. day of ARCHIVE
